$comment: Memory write-intent contract . Deterministic: classifies one user message into a closed intent, extracts the proposition, scope and kind, flags secret / special-category content, and decides the single suggestion bar (memory candidate, conversation instruction, or none). A classification only ever produces a pending candidate: nothing becomes an active memory item without the user accepting it. Candidates are local only (never cloud-synced, never in backups or desktop goldens). Builds on directive-detector.v2 (same primitives, its production detector is called for directives). Lexicon v1 covers zh-Hans and en (and their mix); in other languages only directive-detector global directives reach the memory route. `label` is the human judgement; `expected` is what every client must output exactly. Cases with golden=true are the §9 golden matrix and must equal their label. Clients embed the lexicon through scripts/context-memory-intent-lexicon-gen.mjs.
algorithm: 1 Primitives. Scan only the first directive-detector maxScanCodePoints code points. trim, norm, wordform, term matching per mode, mask, sentence split, isQuestion and the filler-dropping start check are exactly directive-detector.v2 algorithm rules 1–9. detect(s) is the client's production directive detector. Lexicon languages are zh-Hans and en, in that order, each with the mode its directive-detector language has (lexiconModes). has(s, key): some term of lexicon[L][key] matches s in L's mode for some L. dirHas(s, key): same over directive-detector lexicon[L][key] for L in zh-Hans, en; dirHasAny(s, key): over all directive-detector languages. head(s, key): for some L, rule 9 with L's directive-detector fillers and lexicon[L][key] in place of starts.

2 hasExcept(s, key, exKey): per L, substring mode: in norm(s) replace every occurrence of norm(e) (each e of lexicon[L][exKey] in list order, left to right, non-overlapping) by one space, then test norm(term) as a substring; word mode: in wordform(s), for each e in list order repeatedly replace the first occurrence of ' ' + wordform-core(e) + ' ' by ' ' until none is left, then test ' ' + wordform-core(term) + ' '.

3 codeMask(m): find the maximal runs of code points in U+0021..U+007E. A run is code when it contains a codeTokenChars code point, or an ASCII lowercase letter directly followed by an ASCII uppercase letter, or an ASCII letter or digit followed by '.' followed by an ASCII letter. Every code point of a code run becomes U+0020 (length unchanged).

4 Sentences are directive-detector sentences of the scanned text. For each: O = the original code points of its [start, end) range (untrimmed), M1 = the same range of the directive mask, M2 = codeMask(M1), span = trim(O). The first matching step decides the sentence; a sentence matching no step is ignored. (a) has(O, memoryWords) and not has(M2, memoryWords) → ack_or_meta/quoted. (b) has(M2, memoryWords) and has(M2, metaTerms) → ack_or_meta/meta. (c) isQuestion(M1) (directive rule 5, which trims M1 itself): recall/question when (has(M2, memoryWords) and has(M2, recallAddressees)) or has(M2, recallTerms), otherwise the sentence is ignored. (d) has(M2, recallTerms) → recall/recall. (e) hasExcept(M2, deleteTerms, deleteExceptions) → delete_or_supersede/delete. (f) has(M2, supersedeTerms) → delete_or_supersede/supersede. (g) hasExcept(M2, transientTerms, transientExceptions) → transient/transient. (h) head(M2, reminderStarts): detect(span).isDirective → implicit_persist/directive as in (j), else transient/reminder. (i) head(M2, persistStarts) and not head(M2, ackTerms): P = proposition(span); P non-empty and head(P, reminisceStarts) → ack_or_meta/reminisce; anaphorOnly(P) → uncertain/anaphor; else explicit_persist/persist with proposition P, kind kindOf(P), scope global if dirHasAny(M2, globalMarkers), else folder if has(M2, folderMarkers), else conversation if has(M2, conversationMarkers), else unspecified. (j) detect(span).isDirective → implicit_persist/directive. (k) has(M2, implicitMarkers) and dirHas(M2, verbs) and not dirHas(M2, vetoes) and not has(M2, ackTerms) → implicit_persist/loose_directive. (l) has(M2, ackTerms) → ack_or_meta/ack. (m) has(M2, uncertainMarkers) and has(M2, anaphorDirective) → uncertain/anaphor_directive. Implicit results: proposition = span, kind instruction, scope global if ((j)/(h): the detection scope is global; (k): dirHasAny(M2, globalMarkers)), else folder if has(M2, folderMarkers), else conversation.

5 proposition(span), on the span's code points: fold maps ASCII A–Z to a–z and nothing else; a term matches at i when its code points equal the folded code points from i and, for a term of a word-mode language, the next code point is absent or outside Unicode L*/N*/M*. Separators are White_Space and the `separators` code points. Phase 1: repeat { skip separators; when some persistStarts term (any lexicon language) matches go to phase 2; otherwise remove the longest matching term among the zh-Hans and en directive-detector fillers and the zh-Hans and en politePrefixes; when none matches return trim(span) }. Phase 2: remove the longest matching persistStarts term. Phase 3: repeat { skip separators; remove the longest matching linkers term; stop when none matches }. Return trim(rest).

6 anaphorOnly(P): drop trailing separators from trim(P); empty → true; else true when for some L and some anaphorOnly term t: substring mode norm(P') = norm(t), word mode wordform-core(P) = wordform-core(t). kindOf(P): instruction when detect(P).isDirective or, for L in zh-Hans / en, rule 9 accepts P with L's directive fillers and directive starts; else the first of project, goal, preference, identity with head(P, kindStarts[k]) (kindStarts[k] of each L); else fact.

7 Message intent: the decided sentence with the highest rank — delete_or_supersede 80, explicit_persist 70, implicit_persist 60 (+5 when its scope is not conversation), uncertain 50, recall 40, transient 30, ack_or_meta 20; ties keep the earlier sentence. No decided sentence → intent none, rule null, span null.

8 sensitive(text) over the scanned text, unmasked: secret when has(text, secretTerms) or any secretPatterns regex matches (scan all leftmost non-overlapping matches; a pattern with luhn true counts only when the match's ASCII digits pass the Luhn check); else special when has(text, specialTerms); else none. Patterns use ASCII classes and lookarounds only and are case-sensitive.

9 Output {intent, rule, span, proposition, kind, scope, sensitive, blocked, suggestion}. proposition / kind / scope / blocked are null unless the intent is explicit_persist or implicit_persist. blocked = conversation_scope when scope is conversation; else secret / special from sensitive; else too_long when the proposition has more than contentMaxCodePoints code points; else null. suggestion = none when sensitive is secret; memory when the intent persists and blocked is null; conversationInstruction when detect(text).isDirective (the conversation-instruction bar condition on the whole text); none otherwise. One message gets at most one suggestion bar.
10 fingerprint(content) = lowercase sha256 hex of the UTF-8 of canonical(content); canonical = norm(content) with every run of White_Space collapsed to one U+0020 and both ends trimmed.

11 makeCandidate(classification, context): suggestion ≠ memory → skip no_suggestion. context.autoSuggest = false (absent means true) and intent implicit_persist → skip auto_suggest_off (explicit_persist still creates: the user asked). fp = fingerprint(proposition); fp equal to the fingerprint of some activeContents entry → skip duplicate_active. id = UUIDv5(uuidNamespace, messageId + '\n' + fp). The first record (list order) with the same id → skip exists, or with the same fingerprint and status pending → skip duplicate_pending, or with the same fingerprint, status rejected and nowMs < expiresAtMs → skip rejected_recently. Otherwise create a pending record: proposedLayer semantic, proposedKind = kind, content = proposition, scope global → {global, null}; folder → {folder, folderId} or {conversation, conversationId} without folder; unspecified → {folder, folderId} or {global, null} without folder; source {conversation, conversationId, [messageId], observedAtMs = nowMs}; sensitivity normal; confidence from constants by intent; createdAtMs = nowMs; expiresAtMs = nowMs + candidateTtlMs; resolvedAtMs null.

12 accept(record, edit, nowMs): status ≠ pending → error not_pending; nowMs ≥ expiresAtMs → expired; content = trim(edit.content) when given, else the record content; empty → empty; more than contentMaxCodePoints → too_long. Result: the record cleared to accepted, and an item draft {layer = proposedLayer, kind = edit.kind or proposedKind, status active, content, scope = edit.scope or the record scope, source {conversation, conversationId, messageIds, observedAtMs} from the record, sensitivity, confidence = record confidence when content equals the record content, else 1}. The client creates a new Memory Item from the draft through its normal create path; the candidate never turns into the item. Cleared = content '', source {conversation, null, [], null}, resolvedAtMs = nowMs, expiresAtMs unchanged.

13 reject(record, nowMs): status ≠ pending → error not_pending; else cleared to rejected with expiresAtMs = nowMs + candidateTtlMs: only the fingerprint is kept (no body, no source pointers) for short-term de-duplication.

14 sweep(records, activeContents, nowMs), records in order: pending and nowMs ≥ expiresAtMs → expired and purged; pending whose fingerprint is the fingerprint of an activeContents entry → superseded and purged; other pending → kept; rejected with nowMs < expiresAtMs → kept; everything else → purged. Returns keptIds, expiredIds, supersededIds, purgedIds in input order. A store therefore only holds pending and live rejected records.
